title: Documentation obligations — the value of pkit::work-tracking:doc-check, version 1
description: The data point's companion schema (COR-052 point 5; project-management:DEC-053 point 1). The value is the documentation obligations a pull request may owe, before any diff: `check-doc-mapping` applies them to a pull request's diff. The point is `additive`, so entries from different sources are keyed never to collide — a mapping obligation by its mapping rule (`mapping:<code pattern>`, `#<n>` for the n-th rule repeating a pattern), any other by source and what it concerns (`<source>:<document or path>`, by convention). An obligation leaves the point only through the project filler's removal override, with its reason. The version rises only on a change that breaks existing fillers.

source.description: Where the obligation comes from, one enforcement setting per source (DEC-053 point 3): `mapping` for this capability's code-to-doc mapping, which only this capability's own filler supplies; any other lowercase word for a contributed source (`friction`, say), set in the project configuration's `doc_check.sources` and advisory by default.

mapping-obligation.description: One rule of the project's code-to-doc mapping (DEC-015). Met exactly as the mapping always was: the diff touches one of `documents`, or the pull request's `## Doc impact` section names the changed code path or the rule's pattern.

code.description: The rule's gitignore-style pattern over the code; the obligation applies when the diff adds, modifies or renames a file it matches.

documents.description: The documents (paths or gitignore-style patterns) of which any one in the diff meets the obligation.

contributed-obligation.description: An obligation a documentation capability, or the project filler, contributes. One that names a `document` is met only by the page's answer in the diff: a changed file matches `document`; the form of the answer — updated, unchanged with its justification, deferred with its reason — is the core change check's to verify (`pkit friction check`). One that names no `document` is met only when its filler no longer gives it: the filler reads the pull request's head, so a `code-undocumented` obligation leaves the point once a page anchors its `path`. A `## Doc impact` line never meets either.

reason.description: `page-stale`: an anchored page went stale in this change; it names the page as `document`. `code-undocumented`: code nothing documents; it names the code as `path`, and no `document` when it is met by anchoring that code from a page.

document.description: The page (a path, or a gitignore-style pattern) whose change in the diff carries the answer. Required for `page-stale`; absent from a `code-undocumented` obligation whose answer is a page anchoring its `path`.

path.description: The code concerned — required for `code-undocumented`, the code a page must anchor.

description.description: One line a person reads in the check's report.
